Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023 and a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3589928 dated 7/21/2023. An onsite meeting was scheduled with Petro Erie Inc. and the Department which developed this Inspection Report.Individuals present at the onsite meeting:Harry Rhoades -Owner/Operator of Petro Erie Inc.Chris Rhoades -Driver for Harry RhoadesRob Bechtel -PA DEPRick Willey -PA DEPAlan Wolf -PA DEPLucas Eichner -PA DEPSteve Wells -PA DEPThe meeting was started off by Rob Bechtel stating the reason for the meeting and what was discovered during a previous site inspection on 7/21/2023 with violations cited. It was discussed that there is a potential that the discharge of produced fluid from the tank battery may have impacted the Reno, PA public water supply. Mr. Rhoades asked if the pubic water supply was now safe to drink and if regular testing was being conducted. We informed him that the oil and gas program was collecting samples for analysis to determine if the water supply was impacted by oil and gas activity and that the Safe Drinking Water program was working with Venango Water Company related to the public water supply. The discussion with Mr. Rhoades made him aware of the fact that there are more than several concerns with his lease. The Department recommended that he hire an environmental consultant to help him through the cleanup and reporting process of an Act 2 cleanup regarding the discharge of produced fluid and the potential impact of the Reno public water supply. Other violations were discussed regarding the other wells on his lease. Statements that were made by Mr. Rhoades during the meeting:-He is the only owner/operator of Petro Erie Inc-He pumps the wells on the lease himself-One well on the lease is on a timer and pumps when he is not present-Mr. Rhoades does not know what occurred at the site referring to the discharge of produced fluid-Wants the water of the households in Reno tested-Hauled 3 loads of brine, 1 load hauled by Gavin to disposal in OH and 2 loads hauled by Paul Weaver to a frac job in West Virginia-Stated that the tank battery and the impact area was present when he purchased the lease

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2/10/2022 to STL RESOURCES LLC in Grugan Twp, Clinton county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STL RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/10/2022
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 945076
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/10/2022
Comments: On February 10, 2022, DEP representatives Brad Kline and Clark Smith conducted a follow up site inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. The DEP met with STL Resources, and DEP showed STL Resources the area of high conductivity near the middle of the northwest infiltration berm that was found during an inspection on February 2, 2022. The DEP recommends exploring the area to verify if more excavation may be needed. The northwest infiltration berm area was screened with a soil conductivity meter and no new areas of high conductivity were found. STL Resources dug 8 test pits on the well pad to delineate the spill area and determine how deep the excavation will need to be to remove the contaminated pad surface. There was only one open test pit on the pad, the other pits had been backfilled. The conductivity of the side walls of the pit ranged from 400 uS/cm to 700 uS/cm. There was a small pool of water at the bottom of the test pit and the conductivity water was over range of the Oakton multimeter. The maximum conductivity of the meter is 20,000 uS/cm. Soil sample 0651-098 was collected from the test pit. The contaminated soil pile remains on containment at the well pad. STL Resources is still awaiting sample results to be able to dispose of the soil to the landfill. The conductor rig was onsite in the process of drilling the second well cellar and conductor of four. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227 and 3306834.

Report Details

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 996788
Permit API: 117-22129
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 5/30/2023
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an Administrative (ADMIN) inspection of the Seneca Resources - Cruttenden 846 Well Site in response to receipt of a NOV response from the operator on 5/26/23 regarding violations of SWMA 301, 25 Pa Code 78a.56(a) and the violation of CSL 402(b), originally cited 1/11/23 in IR#3486282 and 2/17/23 in IR#3506790. The NOV response state "Per your request in Inspection Report [3486282], non-reportable, de minimis quantities of higher conductivity fluid were transferred by field personnel and truck tires. Using the collection bottle for scale in Photo #13, the puddle from which sample 4427-298 was collected is approximately 160 inches long by 40 inches wide by 1 inch deep, giving a total puddle volume of 87 gallons or 330 liters. Assuming a brine chloride concentration of 115,200 mg/L (chloride concentration averaged across eleven different 26R samples recently collected from eleven different wells in Tioga County), less than 2 gallons of brine would be necessary to produce the reported chloride concentrations in the puddle. The 2-gallon volume of brine is likely an overestimation given that the calculation assumes all the chloride comes from the brine and neglects the appreciable contribution of chloride expected from road salt. The chloride/barium ratio of 765 supports that the puddle is enriched with another source of chloride as the Tioga brine chloride/barium ratio averages around 20 (as calculated from the 26R samples referenced above). Given that the pad material is sourced from the limestone of the Benner through Loysburg Formations at the Salona Quarry in Mill Hall, a quarry frequented by local mineral clubs for its strontianite, strontium leaching from the limestone and concentrating in the clay fractions of the pad material is not unexpected. There was not a release of a reportable quantity of brine.The puddle volume from which sample 4427-295 was collected cannot be estimated as the puddle from which the sample is collected is not identified. Photo #9 refers to multiple puddles with varying levels of conductivity. The reported chloride concentration for sample 4427-295 is 5 times less than the chloride concentration from sample 4427-298. The chloride/barium ratio for this sample is 2,697, indicating that the sample is significantly enriched by a source of chloride other than brine. This puddle is believed to be road salt transfer. As described above, strontium leaching from the limestone and concentrating in the clay fractions of the pad material is not unexpected. There was not a release of a reportable quantity of brine. As a prudent and diligent operator, Seneca reports all reportable spills/releases per the PADEPs regulations. Seneca Operations staff are working with field staff and contractors to continually improve containment maintenance and pad conditions after precipitation events, especially in the winter months when freeze/thaw weather conditions are prevalent."The Operator's response will be uploaded to eFacts and a Compliance Evaluation Inspection will be conducted to evaluate the remediation of the release.Violations of the following regulations are cited as OUTSTANDING against the Cruttenden 846 34HU, API#117-22129 :SWMA 301 25 Pa Code 78a.56(a)The violation of CSL 402(b), originally cited 1/11/23 in IR#3486282 and 2/17/23 in IR#3506790.

Permit API: 129-28077
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Manor Borough
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/19/2025
Comments: On March 19 2025 the Department conducted an inspection of the RWS Development 001 OG Well in regards to an incident reported to the Department of an explosion and fire at the well site on 3/19/2025 at 1:00 pm. Present during the inspection were several representatives from the Manor Volunteer Fire Department, Westmoreland City Fire Department, Jay Niehenke (Kriebel), Ronald Seich (Kriebel) Ben Dickun (Kriebel) and Charles Reaggle (DEP).-This is inspection 1 of a 2 part inspection-The findings are as follows:Upon the Department's arrival to the well site, no active fire was observed. The Department spoke to fire department representative Brian Williams who stated they used approximately 3200 gallons of municipal water from their firetruck as well as Dawn Dish Soap at a 0.6% per gallon concentration to extinguish the fire on site. While onsite, the SDS sheet for Dawn Dish Soap used was sent to the Department electronically by the Fire Department Representative Brian Williams. According to the SDS sheet, "Ecotoxicity- The product is not expected to be hazardous to the environment."Upon inspection of the production equipment, the Department observed damage to the equipment including a hole in the production tank as a result of the incident. Upon inspection of the hole in the production tank, the Department observed a small intermittent trickle of fluid from the production tank hole, down the side of the tank to the ground. A soil conductivity reading was taken directly under the hole in the tank with a reading of OR (over detectable range, >20.0 mS). The Department inquired what the most recent tank level was prior to the incident. Mr. Dickun stated that it was believed to be approximately 2 feet 6 inches from the bottom, however the date and exact measurement was unknown as that information is stored on a computer and was unable to be accessed at the time of the inspection. The Department took a measurement of the of the hole in the tank, which appeared level with the fluid level and obtained a measurement of approximately 2 feet 10.5 inches. While onsite, a truck arrived and began emptying the fluid from the production tank.The Department then assessed the well site to determine impacts resulting from any releases on the site as a result of the explosion/ fire and resulting measures taken to extinguish it. The Department observed a ditch/channel approximately 15 feet behind the well. The ditch appeared to run approximately 180 feet where it terminates just before a stream. The Department observed standing fluid in the ditch/channel in several locations. The Department also observed absorbent pads in the ditch that were reportedly placed placed by the Fire Department. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid in the ditch in several locations with readings of OR, 6.28mS, 5.75mS, and 5.25mS. The conductivity readings appeared to decrease with distance from the well/production tank. No standing fluid was observed in the ditch in approximately the last 45 feet prior to terminating near the stream. There did not appear to be a recent flow path of fluid in the section of ditch from the last location of standing water to the remainder of ditch before the stream. Conductivity readings were taken in this area of the ditch with readings of 0.42mS, 0.34mS, and 0.42mS.The Department then took conductivity readings of the water in the stream. A conductivity reading was taken upstream of where the ditch appears to terminate with a reading of 0.65mS. There appeared to be a large amount of debris and trash in the stream and on the stream bank upstream where this conductivity reading was taken. A conductivity reading was then taken in the stream in the area where the ditch appears to terminate prior to the stream with a reading of 0.90mS. No sheen, discoloration, or foaming was observed in the stream.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/06/2022 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Standing Stone Twp, Bradford county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/06/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 971571
Permit API: 015-21760
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Standing Stone Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/06/2022
Comments: On 11/6/2022, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Jones well site. It was 69 degrees and mostly clear when I arrived on location. Logging activity is being conducted near the well site. The access road has been impacted by the heavy logging equipment. Logging equipment and logs were located on the southwest corner of the pad surface. I discussed the logging operations with the logging equipment owner who was on site when I arrived on location. He is conducting logging operations at the land owner's request. He is about completed at the site and will be cleaning up the pad surface and repairing the road soon. Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. Two erosional channels were witnessed, one on either side of the rock level spreader above the south end of retentive grading/infiltration area 1. PCSM is addressed by one retentive grading/infiltration area.There were two wells staged for production. Both wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. There were three well cellars that were overtopped with water. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The GPUs and production tank had secondary containment. Water in the east GPU secondary containment was field tested for conductivity with an Oakton PCTS 50, the result being over 20.0 mS. The ground immediately north of the GPU was field tested with a Hanna Groline soil test probe for conductivity with the result being 4000 uS. The upper limit of the probe is 4000 uS.I collected water sample 9551 031 from the GPU secondary containment for laboratory analysis SAC 942/aluminum/lithium/bromide. I collected soil sample 9551 032 from the ground immediately north of the GPU for laboratory analysis SAC 530/bromide/lithium/strontium. The release of fluid with elevated conductance to the pad surface constitutes a violation of section 402 of the Clean Streams Law. The department request that Chesapeake performs screening on the pad to determine the extent of the elevated conductance, and that Chesapeake provides the screening data to the department. The department also recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance 78a.66 due to the unknown volume of the release.The department recommends the following: 1. Assess the condition of the rock level spreader located above the south end of infiltration area 1 and repair as necessary.2. Assess the pad surface and access road after logging operations have ceased at the site to ensure that adequate cleanup has been conducted at the site and the affected areas returned to stable condition. 3. Remove the water from and clean the GPU secondary containments and remove the water from the well cellars.I left the site at 15:30 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARMAC RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/04/2023
Violation Code: 78.91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under 25 Pa. Code §§ 78.92—78.98 or an approved alternate method.
Violation ID: 8167223
Permit API: 123-45286
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Warren City
Inspection Type: Plugging(Includes Plugged/Mined Through)
Inspection Date: 12/04/2023
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an active stray gas migration case (CTS# 369563). Previously this well was found to have methane detected outside of the well bore and the operator decided to plug the well. Upon completion of their plugging attempt they inadvertently cemented some of their tubing into the well. Subsequently a camera was ran into the well and bubbles were visibly seen at the top of fluid level. A MSA Altair 5X gas meter was used and determined the bubbles were methane being emitted into the well bore. A violation was issued to the operator for not properly plugging the well. To address this violation the operator had a rig attempt to drill down to approx 550', which is 50' below the surface casing shoe and remove the cemented in tubing at which point another camera run would have taken place to see if the well is still bubbling methane. The rig failed to drill down to 550' and it was decided to cement the remaining tubing into the well. Top of cement is now at 288.23' with approx. 102' of tubing encapsulated within the well bore. ARMAC then contracted Hornburg Drilling to drill and clean out the well-bore to a depth of 560'. At this time the Department is requesting an updated timeline and course of action as to when and how this well will be plugged.

Violation ID: 992056
Permit API: 081-21907
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/18/2023
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions at the site after the reported release of produced fluid to the well pad on 3/3/23. The frac is still on-going on the pad. I met with company man Andrew Briggs upon arriving on location. Two puddles of fluid in the produced fluid off-loading area had an electrical conductivity (EC) of 2.44 and 3.61 mS/cm. The Department recommends vacuuming up this fluid. I told the company man my recommendation at the end of this inspection and he said that he would have the puddles vacuumed up. The puddles in the south travel lane had EC readings of less than 1000 uS/cm. The EC of the stormwater at the north corner of the pad was 795 uS/cm. The well site secondary containment appears to be in good condition. No holes or crushed berms were observed.Violations remain outstanding from the reported release of produced fluid to the pad surface on 3/3/23. Violations will remain outstanding until final approval is issued by the Department that Act 2 remediation standards have been attained.

The Department requests that the operator make repairs to the tank and remediate the impacted area according to state regulations and policies for spills/releases on oil and gas well sites. Comments: On 8/3/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Chesapeake Folta well site. It was 65 degrees and hazy when I arrived on location. Completion Consultant Fletcher Brand explained current operations as follows: Haliburton frac crew MSC-4 was on site completing four recently drilled wells. They were on stage 66 on the 24HC well. They have completed 180 of 271 total stages. Fletcher expects the crew to finish on 8/11/2023. The six existing wells remain shut in for the duration of the drilling and completion process. The crew is monitoring the pressures of the existing wells. During the site inspection, I was accompanied by Chesapeake's company man, Colter Dabney. We viewed the frac operational area, the chemical storage area, and the acid storage area; these were all in the frac operations secondary containment. Twelve 350 barrel brine tanks and the brine unloading area were stationed in secondary containment on the southeast corner of the site. The frac fleet runs on electrical power that is generated by locally acquired natural gas from the existing gas line. A temporary waterline has been installed that is bringing water for the fracking operations; the water being pulled from the Salsman SWW on the Susquehanna River. During the inspection, I did not witness any standing water on the unprotected pad surface. A rolloff waste dumpster on the southwest corner of the site did have a plastic liner installed.Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM has not been installed at the site. A new ESG3 was issued for the site on 5/4/2023. Construction on the ESG3 structures has not been initiated yet.Violations cited in inspection report 3520104 on 3/15/2023 are still outstanding for the site for elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface after drilling operations had been completed.The DEP recommends that Chesapeake uses good chemical handling practices at the site and clean up any spilled chemical as soon as it is discovered.I left the site at 1020 hours.

Permit API: 059-27833
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Richhill Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 07/29/2020
Comments: The Department was made aware on Tuesday, July 21, 2020 by an offset adjacent unconventional well operator of a communication incident impacting the operators well. The adjacent operator reported to the Department that unconventional well, permit number 125-27326, received a measurable transfer of fluid and pressure from the RHL28-KHSM (API 059-27833), an offset unconventional well operated by CNX Gas LLC, currently undergoing hydraulic fracturing. According to the adjacent offset operator, observations of fluid and pressure were observed at the 125-27326 well beginning on or around on July 15, 2020. According to the adjacent offset operator, unconventional well permit number 125-27326, is within the zone of influence of the CNX Gas LLC, RHL28-KHSM (API 059-27833) unconventional well currently undergoing hydraulic fracturing. The adjacent operator reported to the Department that CNX Gas LLC, was notified on July 20, 2020 of the communication incident by the adjacent operator. The Department had previously received an electronic notification from CNX Gas LLC, that stimulation activities would begin on the RHL28-KHSM on Thursday, July 9, 2020 at 6:00 pm. The Department contacted CNX Gas LLC, on Tuesday July 21, 2020 regarding the communication incident. The Department informed CNX Gas LLC, of the notification and reporting requirements required by 78a.73(c). CNX Gas LLC, personnel indicated they are aware of the communication incident and are coordinating with the adjacent operator. To date, the Department has not received an electronic notification of the well communication incident in accordance with 78a.73(c).The Department reviewed the Area of Review (AOR) report deliverables as required by 78a.52a(c), and the as-drilled well plats and well records for the RHL28-KHSM (API 059-27833). According to the as-drilled plats, unconventional well permit number 125-27326 is within the AOR zone of influence of the RHL28-KHSM (API 059-27833). The AOR Summary Report information submitted to the Department on August 9, 2019 for the RHL28-KHSM (API 059-27833) failed to identify 125-27326 as an offset unconventional wells located within the AOR zone of influence.After review of all available information, the Department issuing the following violations. See Notice of Violations section below.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Repsol Oil & Gas Usa Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-02-06
Violation Code: OGA3218.2(A) - CONTAINMENT FOR UNCONVENTIONAL WELLS - SITES - Failure to design and construct unconventional well site to prevent spills to the ground surface and off well site.
Violation ID: 841604
Permit API: 115-22483
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Apolacon Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-02-06
Comments: The Department, Frank Hoehle, DEP O&G WQS and I arrived at the site at 11:39 to conduct a follow up inspection in reference to a production fluid spill that occurred at the site on 1-6-19. The weather conditions are cloudy skies, breezy, with rainfall approaching, and a temperature of 35 degrees Fahrenheit. For additional details pertaining to the production fluid spill, refer to the Department's 1-6-19, 1-9-19, and 1-17-19 inspection reports, Inspection ID#'s 2831500, 2832214, 2832221. We met with Murray Kush, site company man, completions consultant of Repsol, and Dave Coxhead, Site Safety Man, of REM Security. Deep Well Services Rig # 2 is in the process of drilling out hydraulic fracturing plugs. Mr. Kush informed the Department the following. "The rig is drilling out frac plugs on the 3H well. A total of 22 plugs will be drilled out. We are the 20th plug. The 1H is done. Frac plugs will be drilled out on the 7H next. The working tanks and gas buster tanks near the pad entrance contain fluid from the 3H plug drill outs. Brine was used on the 1H well to drill out the plugs. Fresh water is used to drill out the plugs on the 3H well. Trucks are removing water from 1H plug drill outs, out of the offloading station near the production equipment. Containment is the same since the frac. We added containment under the rig. Gel is used to drill out plug parts." In addition to conducting a follow-up inspection at the site, the Department conducted a review of sample results for a water sample collected at the site on 1-9-19. The PADEP Bureau of Laboratories in Harrisburg, PA forwarded the results to the Department on 2-6-19. On 1-9-19, the Department collected a groundwater sample from the swale at the base of the Caprio Pad where the water exhibited elevated levels conductivity on 1-8-18. The Department identified this water sample as Caprio Pad SW-1. Upon review of the Department's groundwater sample results, it was noted that the sample results had elevated concentrations of barium, lithium, manganese, strontium, aluminum, chloride, and iron. Barium was detected above the Act 2, Residential and Non-residential Medium Specific Concentration (MSC) for groundwater of 2,000 micrograms per liter (ug/l) with a concentration of 50,600 ug/l. Lithium was detected above the Act 2, Residential and Non-residential MSC for groundwater of 83 ug/l for Residential, Used Aquifers and for Non-residential, Used Aquifers of 230 ug/l with a concentration of 1,270 ug/l. Manganese was detected above the Act 2, Residential and Non-residential MSC for groundwater of 300 ug/l with a concentration of 8,000 ug/l. Strontium was detected above the Act 2, Residential and Non-residential MSC for groundwater of 4,000 ug/l with a concentration of 38,900 ug/l. Aluminum was detected above the Act 2, Secondary Maximum Contaminant Level (SMCL) of 200 ug/l with a concentration of 41,400 ug/l. Chloride was detected above the Act 2, SMCL of 250,000 ug/l with a concentration of 946,000 ug/l. Iron was detected above the Act 2, SMCL of 300 ug/l with a concentration of 34,400 ug/l. Bromide was detected at a concentration of 7,307.28 ug/l. Calcium was detected at a concentration of 252,000 ug/l. Sodium was detected at a concentration of 389,000 ug/l. Specific See the attached sample results. During the inspection, I utilized a Hanna Groline Soil Test HI 98331 meter, and an Oakton PCTS 50 meter to record specific conductance (conductivity) in water in the sump in the infiltration basin at the toe of fill slope, and in water and damp soil west and slightly up-gradient of the sump, where groundwater seeped to the fill slope. Conductivity readings were in the range of (170-240) microsiemens/cm in the sump, and (700-800) microsiemens/cm in water west of the sump, and (150-200) microsiemens/cm in wet soil west of the sump. See photos. The Department left the site at 12:43.

Barium was detected above the Act 2, Residential and Non-residential Medium Specific Concentration (MSC) for groundwater of 2,000 micrograms per liter (ug/l) with a concentration of 50,600 ug/l. Lithium was detected above the Act 2, Residential and Non-residential MSC for groundwater of 83 ug/l for Residential, Used Aquifers and for Non-residential, Used Aquifers of 230 ug/l with a concentration of 1,270 ug/l. Manganese was detected above the Act 2, Residential and Non-residential MSC for groundwater of 300 ug/l with a concentration of 8,000 ug/l. Strontium was detected above the Act 2, Residential and Non-residential MSC for groundwater of 4,000 ug/l with a concentration of 38,900 ug/l. Aluminum was detected above the Act 2, Secondary Maximum Contaminant Level (SMCL) of 200 ug/l with a concentration of 41,400 ug/l. Chloride was detected above the Act 2, SMCL of 250,000 ug/l with a concentration of 946,000 ug/l. Iron was detected above the Act 2, SMCL of 300 ug/l with a concentration of 34,400 ug/l. Bromide was detected at a concentration of 7,307.28 ug/l. Calcium was detected at a concentration of 252,000 ug/l. Sodium was detected at a concentration of 389,000 ug/l. During the inspection, I utilized a Hanna Groline Soil Test HI 98331 meter, and an Oakton PCTS 50 meter to record specific conductance (conductivity) in water in the sump in the infiltration basin at the toe of fill slope, and in water and damp soil west and slightly up-gradient of the sump, where groundwater seeped to the fill slope. Conductivity readings were in the range of (170-240) microsiemens/cm in the sump, and (700-800) microsiemens/cm in water west of the sump, and (150-200) microsiemens/cm in wet soil west of the sump. properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/13/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 991492
Permit API: 081-21846
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/13/2023
Comments: On April 13, 2023, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident response to a reported spill at the EQT ARO LLC Chapman Bohlin Pad A. The spill of triethylene glycol and production fluid was reported to DEP by Zac Subra from a failed gasket on a reboiler at one of dehydration units onsite. Mr. Subra estimated about 42 gallons spilled outside of containment onto the well pad surface. DEP met with Mr. Subra and Penn E and R who was overseeing the clean up onsite. EQT contractors were just beginning to excavate the area of impact. The area of impact was about 20 ft. x 15 ft. on the southwest side of the dehydration unit. An additional area of impact under the reboiler was visually stained about 4 ft. x 2 ft. The well pad surface was visually impacted and the area had elevated conductivity in the 2,000 uS/cm range. The area to the southwest of the dehydration unit was scraped about an inch deep to remove the visually impacted soil. The area under the reboiler was excavated about 8 inches deep to remove the visually impacted soil. Conductivity of the finished excavation area according to Penn E and R was 500-1200 uS/cm. EQT was planning on having Penn E and R collect confirmatory samples for the cleanup of the spill.On April 14, 2023, EQT ARO LLC provided the DEP a revision on the estimated amount spilled at the dehydration unit to approximately 15-20 gallons. The estimation was revised based on the amount of soil that was excavated and EQT observation of their midstream system monitoring equipment indicating increased moisture content showing some of the release went into the pipeline. The spilling of triethylene glycol and production fluid outside of containment to the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste ManagementAct Section 301. These violations have been immediately corrected.

An additional area of impact under the reboiler was visually stained about 4 ft. x 2 ft. The well pad surface was visually impacted and the area had elevated conductivity in the 2,000 uS/cm range. The area to the southwest of the dehydration unit was scraped about an inch deep to remove the visually impacted soil. The area under the reboiler was excavated about 8 inches deep to remove the visually impacted soil. Conductivity of the finished excavation area according to Penn E and R was 500-1200 uS/cm. EQT was planning on having Penn E and R collect confirmatory samples for the cleanup of the spill.On April 14, 2023, EQT ARO LLC provided the DEP a revision on the estimated amount spilled at the dehydration unit to approximately 15-20 gallons. The estimation was revised based on the amount of soil that was excavated and EQT observation of their midstream system monitoring equipment indicating increased moisture content showing some of the release went into the pipeline. The spilling of triethylene glycol and production fluid outside of containment to the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste ManagementAct Section 301. These violations have been immediately corrected.
